title: Ethics, law & environment
examples: What is the difference between copyright and data protection?
How does throwing old electronics away affect the environment?
Can I use images found online for my school project?

explain.say: Today we are discussing important topics in digital life. We will look at data protection, copyright, and e-waste.

items: Data Protection: Keeping personal information safe.
E-Waste: Dealing with old electronic devices.

explain.say: Data protection laws control how companies use your personal information. You must give permission before they collect it.

draw.text: Data Protection: Need consent for data.

explain.say: Copyright gives the creator legal rights over their original work. This protects things like books or songs.
E-waste refers to discarded electronic equipment. Throwing these items in regular bins is very harmful.
In everyday life, when you take photos with your phone, you are creating copyrighted work. You must respect others' photos too.
A common mistake is sharing private photos without permission. Always ask the owner before sharing someone's personal data.

draw.text: Mistake: Sharing private data without consent.

faq.q: What is the difference between copyright and data protection?
faq.a: Copyright protects the expression of an idea, like a book. Data protection protects personal information about an individual person.
asks: Is personal data the same as copyrighted material?

faq.q: If I find an old laptop, can I just throw it in the regular trash?
faq.a: No, old electronics contain materials that can pollute the environment. They must go to a special e-waste recycling centre.
asks: Where should I dispose of old batteries?
Is e-waste just about big machines?

faq.q: Do I need permission to use a picture I found on Google?
faq.a: You might need permission depending on how you use it. Some images are protected by copyright law.
asks: What if I just use it for school?

faq.q: What is considered 'personal data' under these laws?
faq.a: Personal data includes names, addresses, and phone numbers. It is any information that can identify you as an individual.
asks: Does my email address count as personal data?

faq.q: What are the main materials found in e-waste?
faq.a: E-waste contains valuable metals like gold and copper, but also hazardous materials like lead and mercury.
asks: What is the danger in old electronics?

facts: Data protection laws require organizations to handle personal data responsibly.
Copyright protects the original expression of an idea, not the idea itself.
E-waste contains hazardous materials that pollute soil and water.
Recycling old electronics prevents valuable resources from being lost.

quiz.say: A student writes a poem and posts it online. Another student copies the poem exactly. This is primarily a violation of:
quiz.why: Copyright law protects the unique written expression of the poem.

wrong.0: Fair use allows limited use, but copying the whole poem is too much.
wrong.2: Data protection deals with personal information, not poems.
wrong.3: E-waste only relates to discarded electronics.

quiz.say: A company collects student names and phone numbers without telling the parents. This is a breach of:
quiz.why: Collecting personal data without consent is against data protection rules.

wrong.0: This term is too broad; data protection is the specific law needed.
wrong.2: Copyright is about creative works, not names.

quiz.say: What is the correct way to dispose of an old smartphone?

options.show: Throw it in the household bin.
options.say: Throw it in the household bin.

options.show: Give it to a friend to use.
options.say: Give it to a friend to use.

options.show: Leave it outside for litter pickers.
options.say: Leave it outside for litter pickers.

options.show: Take it to a certified recycling centre.
options.say: Take it to a certified recycling centre.

quiz.why: Certified centres handle toxic materials safely and recover valuable parts.

wrong.0: This releases heavy metals into the ground.
wrong.1: The friend might not know how to safely recycle it later.
wrong.2: Litter pickers are not equipped for electronic waste.
